core_obligations: Reduce the statement to a test against an arbitrary R-module K: it suffices to show that N = M tensor^L K is isomorphic to a module placed in degree 0, which is what the flatness of M means (proof lines 30046-30048).

Use assumption (1) to see that N has nonvanishing cohomology only in degrees at most 0, and invoke the criterion which reduces flatness of N to the vanishing of H^i(N)_f for i negative and of H^i(C) for i less than -1, where C is the cone of multiplication by f on N (proof lines 30049-30053).

For the first condition, compute H^i(N)_f as the cohomology of (M tensor^L R_f) tensor over R_f with (K tensor^L R_f) and use assumption (2) to conclude that it vanishes for i different from 0, where one gets H^0(M)_f tensor K (proof lines 30054-30061).

For the second condition, write C = M tensor^L C' with C' the cone of multiplication by f on K, use the distinguished triangle (K[f])[1] -> C' -> K over fK and the identification M tensor^L K' = M tensor^L R over fR tensor over R over fR K' for modules K' annihilated by f, and apply assumption (3) to conclude that C has nonzero cohomology only in degrees 0 and -1 (proof lines 30061-30079).
proof_roadmap: Test flatness of M against an arbitrary module K and reduce to the two vanishing conditions of the criterion in the form stated in the section (proof lines 30046-30053).
Compute the f-localizations of the cohomology of N through M tensor^L R_f and K tensor^L R_f, and use assumption (2) to make them vanish in negative degrees (proof lines 30054-30061).

Express the cone of multiplication by f on N as M tensor^L times the cone on K and use the triangle with K[f] and K over fK together with assumption (3) to make its cohomology vanish below degree -1 (proof lines 30061-30079).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a flatness criterion for an object M of D(R) given two local conditions: vanishing cohomology above degree 0, and the derived tensor products with R_f and with R over fR being flat modules placed in degree 0 (statement lines 30032-30043). The proof has to check two distinct and not obviously related conditions for the object N = M tensor^L K, namely the vanishing of the f-localized cohomology in negative degrees, which is computed through the factorization of the derived tensor product along R_f, and the vanishing of the cohomology of the cone of multiplication by f below degree -1, which is computed by writing the cone as a derived tensor product with the cone on K and using the triangle with K[f] and K over fK (proof lines 30054-30079). The two hypotheses on M are used in exactly one place each, and the argument is carried out for an arbitrary test module K, so the reduction is the substantive step. The counted span refers to one lemma and one section of this chapter; the computations themselves are inside the span.
